topic: Why do phone batteries get worse over time?
title: The Real Reason Your Battery Gets Worse 🔋
description: Your battery isn't just 'old': lithium gets trapped in a growing SEI layer on the graphite and never comes back.
Heat and sitting at 100% speed it up. Apple rates ~80% capacity after 500 cycles (1,000 on iPhone 15).
sources: Apple – Maximizing Battery Life and Lifespan (above 35 °C can permanently damage capacity): https://www.apple.com/batteries/maximizing-performance/

AppleInsider – iPhone 15 battery rated for 1,000 cycles; iPhone 14 and earlier, 500: https://appleinsider.com/articles/24/02/20/apple-says-the-iphone-15-battery-is-more-durable-than-it-originally-thought
Battery Design – SEI growth (irreversible lithium loss, faster at high temperature and high state of charge): https://www.batterydesign.net/chemistry/solid-electrolyte-interphase/sei-growth/
Ionworks – Batteries 101: degradation (loss of lithium inventory, heat, high SOC): https://docs.ionworks.com/guide/batteries-101/degradation

beats.narration: Your phone battery is quietly *eating itself*.
Charging pushes lithium ions into the graphite. Using the phone sends them back.
But over time, some ions get stuck in a crust that keeps growing on the graphite.
That crust is called the SEI layer, and it *never* gives them back.
Fewer free ions means less energy.
After 500 full cycles, older iPhones keep about *80%*.
Apple now rates the iPhone 15 for *1,000* cycles.
Two things make the crust grow faster: heat, and sitting at 100% for hours.
Apple warns that above *35 degrees* Celsius, the damage can be permanent.
